html:
The Wanapum are a Sahaptin-speaking people of the Columbia River in central Washington state, living mainly around Priest Rapids. They fished the river's salmon runs, dug roots and traded with the Yakama, Palouse and other Plateau peoples.

The prophet Smohalla was a Wanapum. From the 1850s he taught the Washani or Dreamer religion, which told his followers to reject farming and white ways and keep to the land as it was. The Wanapum never signed a treaty with the United States and never moved to a reservation.

In the 20th century the Hanford nuclear site took part of their land, and the Priest Rapids Dam flooded their village area. About 60 Wanapum still live near the dam. Neighbours: Columbia.
